definition: In this historical context, an incantation is a spoken magical formula used prominently in trying to appease or influence spirits. It is contrasted with prayer and linked to acts of propitiation rather than adoration.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Demonolatry; pinned source text

reasons: The packet supports incantation only as something that figures prominently in demonolatry, not as a general “spoken magical formula.”
“Influence spirits” is broader than the packet’s wording; the source supports propitiation of spirits and minor adoration, not a general influence claim.
The packet does not state that an incantation is a “spoken magical formula”; it only says that “incantation rather than prayer figures prominently” in the context of spirit-worship/propitiation.

The packet supports the contrast with prayer and the connection to propitiation over adoration, but it does not explicitly support the added phrasing about “trying to appease or influence spirits” as a defining characterization.
